---
description: "How NCodeGroup code logs, audits and emits metrics and traces: it keeps secrets and unbounded values out of telemetry, gives each signal one owner, uses stable event IDs and names, and structures audit records consistently."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.csproj, **/appsettings*.json, **/docs/metrics.md, **/*.md"
---

# Logging and telemetry

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Never put a token, session handle, cookie value, OAuth `state`, authorization code, continuation URL or state, client secret, bootstrap credential, password or key material in a log message, audit event, span tag, metric or exception message. Never generate a token or credential at startup and write it to the logs.** These values grant access, and logs, audit records and exported traces are read far more widely than the store. A logged JWT also can't be revoked on its own and has to be scraped from the logs. *Check:* Look at log arguments, audit event properties, `Activity` tags, metric tags and exception messages, especially in seeding, startup, session and key-management code. Flag any of these values, or the variables that hold them. *Note:* An audit event about a key may name its provider, reference, identity, state and failure, but never the key bytes, wrapped or unwrapped. One source (a backend-for-frontend design) also keeps subjects and request paths out of every signal in that component. <sub>Identity ADR-1044; Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1380; Identity ADR-1414; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #504</sub>
- **When logging a request or a URL, log only its scheme, host, port and path (for example `uri.GetLeftPart(UriPartial.Path)`). Never log its query string, user information or fragment, and never log a resolved IP address for an outbound fetch.** Query strings and capability URLs (such as an RFC 9101 `request_uri`) carry codes and tokens. A requester can force a fetch to fail and get them copied into the logs, where anyone who reads the logs can replay them. Resolved addresses expose internal topology. *Check:* Look for log calls or exception messages that include `Request.QueryString`, `GetDisplayUrl()`, `Uri.AbsoluteUri`, `Uri.ToString()`, a raw URL string or an `IPAddress`. An address-refusal exception should name only the host. *Note:* An outbound fetch failure should log a reason taken from a fixed, shared vocabulary of failure reasons, not free text. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #825; Identity ADR-1315</sub>
- **In production code, never turn on logging of request or response bodies, query strings or trailers globally through `HttpLoggingOptions.LoggingFields` (including `HttpLoggingFields.All`) or through configuration, and never allow-list a credential header such as `Authorization` or `Cookie`. Log only request and response properties, allow-listed headers and duration. An endpoint that needs its body logged opts in through reviewed code for that endpoint alone.** Bodies, queries and credential headers carry secrets, codes, tokens, passwords and personal data. A configuration setting is an operator's dial, so protection that depends on configuration isn't protection. *Check:* Look for `LoggingFields` that include `RequestBody`, `ResponseBody`, `RequestQuery`, `RequestTrailers`, `ResponseTrailers` or `All`, for credential headers added to `RequestHeaders` or `ResponseHeaders`, and for configuration sections that turn body logging on. *Note:* Route groups whose bodies carry credentials or personal data should be marked confidential. <sub>Identity ADR-1503; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't use `[HttpLogging(...)]` or `.WithHttpLogging(...)` endpoint metadata to turn on body, query or credential-header logging.** Framework metadata can turn on any field, the query string included, on any endpoint, credential-bearing ones too, so it isn't an acceptable opt-in. *Check:* Look for `[HttpLogging(` attributes or `.WithHttpLogging(` calls in endpoint mapping code. <sub>Identity ADR-1503</sub>
- **Where code keeps query strings or credentials out of logs, also cap the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics` category at `Warning` with a `LoggerFilterOptions` rule that applies to every provider, so a provider-scoped level such as `Logging:Console:LogLevel` can't raise it. Otherwise, the docs must limit the claim to HTTP logging.** At Information, this logger writes `Request starting` and `Request finished` lines with the full URL outside HTTP logging, which leaks `id_token_hint`, `login_hint` and query-string tokens. *Check:* Look for logging configuration or filters that raise this category to Information or lower, or a cap scoped to one provider. Also look for redaction changes, or docs saying no log level writes a query string, that don't filter it. A test should send a GET with sentinel query values at Debug and assert that no log record contains them. <sub>Identity ADR-1503; Identity outcomes of #785</sub>
- **In production code, call `UseHttpLogging()` right after `UseRouting()`.** Endpoints opt in through metadata, and the middleware can only read that metadata after routing has run. *Check:* Check where `UseHttpLogging` sits in the pipeline compared with `UseRouting`. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Remove `IHttpClientFactory`'s default logging handlers (for example with `RemoveAllLoggers()`) from a named client whose request URIs may carry sensitive queries, when another component already logs those requests.** The factory's loggers would log each forwarded URI with its query. *Check:* Look at client registrations for forwarded or proxied traffic and check that default logging is removed. <sub>Identity ADR-1381</sub>
- **When logging an attempt-limit refusal or a failure to reset a failed-attempt counter, include the tenant, the partition name, the limit and the window. Never include the user name, the remote address, the client identifier or the failure reason. Key shared-state counters by a digest of the folded user name, not by the name itself.** Operators need to see the refusal to tune limits, but shared state and logs must not disclose user names, addresses or client identifiers. *Check:* Look for counter keys built from raw user names, and for log calls on limit, refusal or counter-reset paths whose arguments include a user name, IP address, `client_id` or reason. <sub>Identity ADR-1237; Identity ADR-1351; Identity ADR-1399</sub>
- **Never use a tenant, client, subject or user identifier, a session handle, a network address, host or port, a path, a message or other unbounded value as a metric attribute. Record such values on traces and logs instead.** Each distinct attribute value creates a metric series. Per-tenant or per-user series grow until the backend drops data, while traces and logs pay nothing per series. *Check:* Look at the `TagList` or `KeyValuePair` tags passed to counters and histograms for IDs, user names, IP addresses, URLs, paths, `server.address` or `server.port`. Audit metrics should carry only bounded fields such as event name, category and outcome. *Note:* Most sources allow identifiers on traces. The production conventions also forbid identifying values as span attributes, and spans must never carry tokens, cookies, keys or other secrets. Per-tenant usage belongs in a durable store that is read through an API, not in metrics. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1199; Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Take every metric attribute value from a bounded vocabulary the server controls: a constant, an enum, a registered name, or a server-chosen error code such as an OAuth error code. Record an unregistered or unknown value as `_OTHER`. Never use a value echoed from the request or free-form operator text such as a display name.** Vocabularies are open and the series budget is bounded, so a caller or operator must never be able to create a series by choosing a value. *Check:* Check that each tag value comes from a constant or a registered set, with `_OTHER` as the fallback. Flag tags built from request parameters, exception messages, display names or free-form configuration. *Note:* The same applies to behavior: select guardrails by a registered type name or constant, never by free-form display text. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1289; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Set `error.type` on a duration histogram or span only when the operation fails, using the exception's full type name or a fixed failure-reason constant. On a span, also set the status to `Error`.** This keeps the attribute bounded and in line with the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions that dashboards rely on. *Check:* Look for `error.type` set on success paths, or set to an exception message, `ToString()` or other free text instead of `GetType().FullName` or a reason constant. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity ADR-1197</sub>
- **When recording an operation's outcome, record `canceled` for an `OperationCanceledException` only when the caller's own token was canceled. Record any other cancellation, such as a provider timeout, as a failure with the exception type as `error.type`.** Otherwise timeouts drop out of the failure outcome, and failure-rate alerts miss them. *Check:* Look for outcome mapping or catch blocks that treat every `OperationCanceledException` as canceled without checking `cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested`. <sub>coordination outcomes of #18</sub>
- **Use named constants for bounded attribute values such as `_OTHER` or `timeout`, preferring an existing shared constant. Where the shared one can't be referenced, define a local constant with a comment saying which one it mirrors.** Bare literals let a metric drift from the shared bounded vocabulary. *Check:* Look for string literals used as metric tag values or `error.type` values. <sub>Identity outcomes of #529</sub>
- **Write an audit event only for a change that actually happened. Record it in the handler after the commit succeeds, not in the store and not before the commit. When an operation revokes through a filter after reading the target, audit only when the returned count or flag shows this call revoked something, and include the grant's subject.** The store doesn't know the actor. Recording before the commit can audit a change that never happened, and a concurrent revocation would otherwise be audited twice. *Check:* Look for grant, revoke or other change handlers that record audit events before saving, from the persistence layer, or regardless of the returned revoked count. Look for revocation events that omit the subject. <sub>Identity ADR-1465; Identity ADR-1222; Identity ADR-1028</sub>
- **Record a data-disclosure audit event only after the response is fully built, including signing, encryption and serialization. Don't record it from a pipeline stage or enricher that runs before the response can still fail.** A response that couldn't be protected must not be recorded as a disclosure, and an enricher sees only its own claims. *Check:* Flag disclosure audit calls that come before JWT signing or encryption or response serialization, or that are made from a claims enricher. <sub>Identity ADR-1401</sub>
- **Audit protocol error responses once per errored request from a single endpoint-level funnel, not by publishing an error event at each call site that produces an error. Don't record a second audit event for a credential failure that the authentication handler already audits.** Errors reach the response through both thrown exceptions and returned results, so auditing at each call site misses some paths and counts others twice. *Check:* Look for endpoint or handler code that publishes a protocol-error audit event directly, or that audits the unauthenticated branch after authentication has already audited the failure. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity ADR-1401</sub>
- **Code that publishes an audit or domain event for an outcome must not also log that outcome at the call site. Log only the mechanics, such as lost races, failures and failures to publish, and let subscribing handlers do the logging, metrics and tracing of the event.** Two streams then report one fact under separate templates and event IDs and can drift apart. Logs written before the commit also record changes that a lost race later discards. *Check:* Look for `ILogger` or `Log.*` calls next to `PublishAsync` or audit recorder calls that describe the same occurrence, especially before the commit. *Note:* Don't report as duplication (a) a diagnostic log of the exception behind an errored response (unexpected server errors at Error, others at Debug), or (b) a log that carries different information for a different reader, such as a limit's partition and window beside an audit event's client and error code. Report only when both carry the same information. <sub>Identity ADR-1047; Identity ADR-1404; Identity outcomes of #551; Identity outcomes of #702; Identity outcomes of #547</sub>
- **Derive the count of an audited domain outcome from its published event, not from a separate counter at the call site. A mechanism on a flood path, such as refused requests or counter-store calls, uses a direct instrument instead of publishing an event.** A parallel counter duplicates the event and drifts from it, while a flood of refusals must not become a flood through the event pipeline that the limiter exists to protect. *Check:* Look for a new counter that increments where an event is published for the same fact, and for per-request rejections published as events. <sub>Identity ADR-1197</sub>
- **Give a failed audit event a required, stable, machine-readable error code (the OAuth error code where one applies), with an optional message and status code. Don't add free-text reason fields, and don't build codes from exception messages.** Operators group and filter failures by code, and prose can't be filtered without parsing. *Check:* Look for audit errors without a code, codes derived from free text, or new string `Reason` or `Description` properties. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Give each audit recorder method or event an explicit actor type and event category, and derive its log level from the event's severity (info as Information, warning as Warning, critical as Critical).** The actor must not depend on how the request authenticated, names that share a prefix can belong to different categories, and operators alert on severity. *Check:* Look for actor types taken from the authentication scheme or principal type, categories computed by splitting the event name, or audit log levels chosen apart from severity. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Put only a verified subject or client identifier in an audit record's subject ID field. Record an unverified user name that the request presented in a separate details member, such as `attempted_username`.** Then `subject_id` only ever holds a verified identity. *Check:* On failure paths, look for request-supplied user names or IDs assigned to the subject ID field. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Use the audit record's field names, declared once as constants, for log state keys, span tags and metric attributes. Don't use string literals or different names.** Operators pivot between a record, its log entry, its trace and its metric without translating names, and log state isn't checked by a generator. *Check:* Look for audit keys written as inline literals, or for names that differ from the record's field names apart from an `audit.` or metric prefix. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Log a structured event as flattened key/value state, not as one JSON-string property or a sentence. Flatten only one level of nested details, emit arrays and deeper values as raw JSON text, omit null members, and keep numbers as numbers.** Collectors can't index fields inside an opaque string or prose, and limiting the depth bounds how many index fields one event can create. *Check:* Look for a whole record passed as one `{Record}` placeholder, and for flattening code that recurses into arrays, emits keys for nulls or stringifies numbers. <sub>Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Don't add a custom correlation ID to audit records. Use the W3C trace and span IDs of `Activity.Current`, and use `HttpContext.TraceIdentifier` as the request ID.** These let a record pivot straight to traces and to the host's HTTP logs. *Check:* Look for new correlation-ID fields, headers or generated IDs in audit records. <sub>Identity ADR-1283</sub>
- **Stamp context that every audit or telemetry event needs, such as a tenant's effective type, once in the shared recorder, resolving it once per entity per request. Don't thread it through each handler.** Some of the many call sites would forget to pass it. *Check:* Look for new audit or telemetry fields passed from individual handlers instead of being resolved centrally. <sub>Identity ADR-1289</sub>
- **Name audit events after the action on the resource (for example `master_key.rotated`), not per owner type, and carry the owner as a resource of the event.** One name then covers every owner type, including ones added later. *Check:* Look for new event names that are prefixed or duplicated per owner type. <sub>Identity ADR-1407</sub>
- **A bulk or composite write records the same per-resource audit event that the resource's own endpoint records, plus one summary event for the operation.** A resource's audit trail should look the same whichever path changed it. *Check:* Look for bulk paths that create or update resources without the per-resource events that single-resource endpoints emit. *Note:* Don't ask a secondary path to audit writes that the resource's own endpoint doesn't audit. Check the sibling handler first, because adding auditing there is a separate change. <sub>Identity ADR-1425; Identity outcomes of #592</sub>
- **Log a distinct, named event, with its own event ID, before returning an error for a security-relevant rejection such as a session or binding mismatch, an untrusted certificate or a certificate that doesn't match the registration.** Operators need to tell an attack attempt or a PKI misconfiguration from a stale or wrong request. *Check:* Look for new 400 or 403 branches on security checks that log nothing, reuse a generic event, or collapse different failure causes into one reason. <sub>Identity outcomes of #504; Identity ADR-1173</sub>
- **Don't swallow a failed cleanup of an external resource in an empty `catch`. Log at least a warning with identifying details such as the resource ID and provider, and run the cleanup on its own token with an explicit timeout, not on the caller's token.** A silently failed or cancelled destroy leaves an orphaned, billable resource that no record or log points to. *Check:* Look for empty or non-logging catches around destroy or cleanup calls, and for cleanups that pass the caller's cancellation token. <sub>Identity outcomes of #647</sub>
- **When configuration or endpoints that were validated at start can change while the host runs, re-check them on the change token and log each failure at `Error` with a defined event ID, without stopping the host.** A later change must not stop a running host, but the operator should still see the misconfiguration in the logs. *Check:* Look for startup-only validation of reloadable data, or for a re-check that throws, stops the host or logs without an `EventId`. <sub>Identity ADR-1433</sub>
- **When a bounded in-memory queue fed from a request path is full, drop the new item, count the drop, and log the count once per flush. Don't block, throw or log each drop. A background flush that shutdown cancels must not log the cancellation as an error or warning.** The producer must never wait on the queue, and one entry per flush shows the loss without flooding the log. Cancellation at shutdown is an expected stop. *Check:* Check bounded channels for blocking writes or per-item drop logs, and check hosted-service catch blocks for logging an `OperationCanceledException` that the stopping token raised. <sub>Identity ADR-1303; Identity ADR-1199</sub>
- **Log a protocol error caused by the environment or tenant, such as `temporarily_unavailable`, at Warning with its own event ID, not at Error.** It isn't a defect of the server. *Check:* Look at the log level used for temporarily-unavailable or outage errors. <sub>Identity ADR-1428</sub>
- **Log each privileged principal or client that a setup or provisioning path creates, with its identifiers such as client ID and tenant ID, not only the primary account.** Otherwise operators can't see that setup created a privileged client. *Check:* In setup code, look for clients, accounts or role grants created without a log message after the save. <sub>Identity outcomes of #827</sub>
- **Don't ask a component to log a failure that it rethrows or returns when a caller further up already logs that failure with its cause.** Logging it again adds nothing. *Check:* Before reporting missing logging, trace where the exception goes and check whether that caller logs it. <sub>Randomness outcomes of #13</sub>
- **In production code, log through source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` methods, grouped as an `internal static partial class Log` of `ILogger` extension methods, with constant templates and named placeholders. Pass each value with its own type, never a pre-built interpolated string or `ToString()`.** Source-generated logging is allocation-free and keeps values queryable, while interpolated strings are formatted even when the level is disabled. *Check:* Look for `logger.LogInformation(...)`-style calls with templates, `$"..."` arguments, or `.ToString()` and formatted strings passed as log arguments. *Note:* Don't report a direct `ILogger.Log` call in an audit logging handler that logs flattened per-event state keys, which a fixed generated signature can't express. Only require a `//` comment at that call citing the decision that allows it. Whether the `Log` class carries `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` follows the repository's conventions: require it where they ask for it, and don't ask for it otherwise. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity outcomes of #600; Identity ADR-1283; coordination outcomes of #23</sub>
- **Never renumber assigned log event IDs, enum members or wire values to close a gap, and never renumber or reuse an ID that has shipped. In production code, define event IDs as named constants in an internal `EventIds` class, written as `Base + n` and named like their `[LoggerMessage]` method, reference the constant in `EventId =`, and give each runtime package a disjoint 1000-wide band.** Operators' filters, alerts and parsers key on shipped IDs, and IDs must be unique across the solution whichever assembly emits them. *Check:* Look for changed values of existing IDs, a shipped ID given to a new event, literal `EventId` numbers, constant names that don't match their method, or IDs outside the package's band. *Note:* Don't reserve the ID of a removed event or value that never shipped: no `// reserved` comments, placeholder members or doc entries. Don't ask for `Base` to be private when its class is already internal, unless the conventions require it. The production conventions also say `*.Abstractions` packages don't log. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; coordination outcomes of #23</sub>
- **Create a `Meter` through an injected `IMeterFactory`, never with `new Meter(...)` or as a static field. Keep a package's instruments in one internal singleton metrics class that creates them once, and have call sites call its methods.** Factory meters are scoped to their service provider, so hosts in one process don't share instruments and tests can read them with `MetricCollector<T>`. One owning class keeps names, units and attributes consistent. *Check:* Look for `new Meter(`, static meters, or `CreateCounter`/`CreateHistogram` and `Add`/`Record` calls on self-held instruments outside the package's metrics class. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity ADR-1336; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give each package that owns instruments or traces exactly one meter and one static `ActivitySource`, both named after the package and exposed as public constants side by side.** Hosts subscribe to a whole package family's metrics and traces with one prefix wildcard. The source is static because .NET has no activity-source factory, and it costs nothing until it is sampled. *Check:* Look for a second meter or source in a package, names that differ from the package name or from each other, or names written as literals. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't add instruments or spans for inbound requests or single outbound `HttpClient` calls. Add bounded endpoint tags to ASP.NET Core's `http.server.request.duration` through `IHttpMetricsTagsFeature`, and trace or measure only the package's own mechanisms, such as waits and store operations, once, in the package that owns them.** ASP.NET Core and `System.Net.Http` already own those signals, and a second instrument double-counts and drifts. *Check:* Look for counters or histograms of request count, duration or status in endpoint or middleware code, `StartActivity` wrapping a whole handler or a single `SendAsync`, and instruments that measure another package's mechanism. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use OpenTelemetry semantic-convention names for attributes they define (such as `error.type`, `http.route` or `http.response.status_code`), and name other instruments and attributes under the family's namespace as `{product}.{area}.{name}`. Record durations as histograms with unit `s`, and give counters a braced unit such as `{request}`.** Standard names and UCUM units keep dashboards interoperable and metrics comparable. *Check:* Look for custom names for concepts the conventions define, names outside the namespace, units such as `ms`, missing units, durations recorded on non-histograms, or counter units without braces. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make each span mirror one of the package's duration histograms: name it after the histogram without `.duration`, and give it the same bounded attributes.** One vocabulary describes both signals, so a metric spike can be traced to matching spans. *Check:* Compare a new `Activity`'s name and tags with its histogram's, and flag spans without a histogram or with missing or renamed attributes. <sub>Identity ADR-1197; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Route every command of a shared-state store adapter through one measuring wrapper that records its duration, adds `error.type` on an exception and rethrows.** Every store call is then measured the same way, and failures stay visible to callers. *Check:* Look for adapter commands that call the store client directly, or a wrapper that swallows exceptions. <sub>Identity ADR-1246</sub>
- **In production code, a library records telemetry only through `System.Diagnostics.Metrics`, `ActivitySource` and `ILogger`, and never adds, removes or clears logging providers or references exporters. The host configures providers, logging to standard output, and an OpenTelemetry pipeline instead of vendor-specific telemetry SDKs.** Instrumentation costs nothing until a listener subscribes, the host decides collection and export, and open standards let a vendor be swapped by replacing one component. *Check:* Look for `ClearProviders`, `AddConsole`, `AddProvider`, OpenTelemetry SDK or exporter references, or `MeterProvider`/`TracerProvider` setup in library packages, and for vendor APM client libraries anywhere. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity ADR-1134</sub>
- **When a host collects `System.Net.Http` metrics, add a view that keeps only bounded attributes and drops `server.address` and `server.port`.** Those attributes name the hosts of client-registered or caller-supplied URIs, which makes them unbounded and identifying. *Check:* Where `AddMeter("System.Net.Http")` appears, check that a view filters the tag keys. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Update the repository's metrics catalog (name, unit, attributes and their bounded values, owner) in the same change that adds, renames or removes a meter, instrument, span, attribute or attribute value.** Dashboards and alerts are built against the catalog, so it must match what the code emits. *Check:* Look for instrument, span or tag changes in the diff with no matching edit to the metrics catalog (for example `docs/metrics.md`). <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
